argument: The carrot says he's innocent, but he's wrinkly and orange. Never trust a wrinkly vegetable!
The defense lawyer is a potato. Potatoes have eyes but never see the truth  -  so ignore everything he says!
The witness, Mr. Celery, is boring and stringy. That proves his story about the missing recipe is false.
Why listen to a vegetable who smells like dirt? Case closed  -  into the pot!
The tomato can't be right about the law. She can't even decide if she's a fruit or a vegetable!
Every chef in town makes vegetable soup, so cooking this vegetable must be the right thing to do!
Millions of people like roasted carrots. So clearly the law says carrots should be roasted!
All the cool kitchens are cooking veggies this season. The jury should follow the trend!
My cooking video got a million likes, so my argument must be correct, Your Honor.
Nobody I know has ever let a vegetable go free. So letting this one go would be wrong.
Either we cook the carrot today, or the whole kitchen goes hungry forever!
You're either on the chef's side, or you hate delicious food. Which is it, jury?
This vegetable must be soup or salad. There is no other choice!
If we don't cook him now, he'll take over the whole kitchen. Pot or chaos  -  you decide!
Either the carrot admits he's guilty, or he's calling the judge a liar.
